Triggers.value: Other people expressing anger, even calmly

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Situations that might make me feel happy or hopeful

Threat.value: I find it harder to feel safe at night than during the day
I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people

Memory.value: When I remember the event I feel intense shame
When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.
I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order

Negative Appraisals.value: My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed
I feel isolated and set apart from others
I should have protected others and I failed

vignette: Ravi, a 35-year-old South Asian tax consultant married to his high school sweetheart, had always been driven by a sense of duty and compassion. His decision to volunteer as a relief worker in a war-torn region was born from this same motivation-to help those suffering. However, the experience left him with indelible marks that continued to haunt him long after he returned home. The traumatic event itself was seared into Ravi's memory. He had been in the middle of distributing supplies when an explosion occurred nearby, sending smoke and debris everywhere. The smell of smoke lingered as he witnessed people struggling to escape, many of whom did not make it. This visceral experience made even mundane triggers-like the scent of burning leaves or attending a colleague's funeral-a potent reminder of that day. Since returning from his deployment, Ravi found himself constantly on edge. Any hint of fire or smoke immediately triggered a flood of memories and intense feelings of shame and confusion. He would often cover his face with his hands when these triggers occurred, hoping to shield himself from the overwhelming emotions. This response had grown into a more generalized avoidance; he now avoided not just the site where the event took place but any situation that might evoke similar sensations or remind him of the trauma. The difficulty in concentrating was another significant challenge for Ravi. He found it increasingly hard to focus at work, which required meticulous attention to detail and numerical precision. The slightest noise-a phone ringing, a door slamming-would startle him, plunging him back into that moment of chaos. As a result, his performance at work suffered, leading to tense discussions with supervisors who were unaware of the underlying issues. Ravi's nights were particularly challenging; he found it nearly impossible to feel safe in the darkness. The memory of the event would replay in his mind, causing his body to reenact the positions and sensations from that day. He felt confused about the sequence of events, as if the memories were jumbled together without a clear timeline. This confusion compounded his sense of shame and failure. His beliefs about the world had been shattered by this experience. Ravi was certain he should have done more to protect those around him and failed in his duty. These negative appraisals led him to withdraw from social gatherings and avoid situations where he might feel happy or hopeful, as any positive emotions only heightened his sense of isolation and failure. Ravi's avoidance behaviors extended to even everyday events that reminded him of the trauma. For example, a casual mention of a funeral at work could send him spiraling into distress, further reinforcing his belief that he should have done more. This vicious cycle of triggers leading to maladaptive strategies, which in turn exacerbated his negative appraisals and threat perceptions, was tightening its grip on Ravi. The realization that these symptoms were becoming unbearable finally compelled Ravi to seek help. He was most afraid of reliving the trauma and feeling powerless again, but he also hoped for a way to reclaim control over his life and find some semblance of peace. The combination of his deteriorating work performance and increasing isolation had become too much to bear on his own. In therapy, Ravi began to unravel how specific triggers led him down a path of avoidance and heightened threat perceptions, while the memories he struggled with reinforced his shattered beliefs about himself and the world. He was eager to find strategies that could help him manage these overwhelming feelings and restore some semblance of normalcy in his daily life.
